H0.text: Scope (a definition, the author 10 Nov): the theory is free linearised gravity at order G^0 on Minkowski space, d = 4, the free helicity-2 curvature net on the TT Fock space; the region is the unit ball; the state is a stationary magnetic multipole, l >= 2

H1.text: (A1) the ball's states are the image of the world's states under one normal unital completely positive map Phi: M -> B(F)

H2.text: (A2) no signalling: Phi(M) commutes with every curvature observable in the causal complement of the diamond

H3.text: (A3) M contains the interior curvature observables: a normal unital *-homomorphism iota: A(D) -> M with Phi iota = id

H4.text: (GEO) the gravitational side of the second-order first law is the extremal value of (Area - 2 Volume)/4G, a diffeomorphism-invariant functional of the metric

H5.text: (EIN) the family g_eps solves the vacuum Einstein equations through O(eps^2); only the second-order Hamiltonian constraint is used

I1.text: Ciolli-Longo-Ruzzi Thm 4.5: on R(H), H standard and factorial, S(coherent state of k || vacuum) = -Im(k, P_H i log Delta_H k) for every vector k; literal for k in Dom(log Delta_H) (Cor. 2.3)
I1.locator: arXiv 1906.01707 Thm 2.2, Cor. 2.3, Prop. 2.4-2.5, Thm 4.5 (pdf p7-10, p21); read line by line, PRINT_READ.md I1

I1b.text: Araki: the relative entropy is defined by the relative modular operator and is lower semicontinuous (consumed inside I1)
I1b.locator: Araki, Publ. RIMS 11 (1976) 809, eq. (1.4); statement read, proof not read, PRINT_READ.md I1

I3.text: Uhlmann monotonicity for a unital 2-positive Schwarz map, first state a vector state of a cyclic vector
I3.locator: Reible arXiv 2501.04564 Thm IV.3.7 (pdf p68-71); proof read line by line except its textbook inequalities and Sec. III.4, PRINT_READ.md I3

I4.text: Hislop-Longo and Longo-Morsella: modular group and coherent-state relative entropy of the massless scalar on the ball (used only by the second proof of M)
I4.locator: CMP 84 (1982) 71 Thm 1-2, Cor. 2; arXiv 2012.00565 Thm 4.7, 5.4, Cor. 5.5; read, coefficient pi D re-derived, PRINT_READ.md I4-I5

T6.text: Tomita-Takesaki theorem: J M J = M' and Delta^{it} M Delta^{-it} = M (Bratteli-Robinson 1, Thm 2.5.14; book not on file)

T7.text: Takesaki: a faithful normal state is KMS at beta = -1 for exactly one sigma-weakly continuous group, its modular group; the condition may be checked on a sigma-weakly dense invariant *-subalgebra (Bratteli-Robinson 2, Thm 5.3.10 with Def. 5.3.1 and Cor. 5.3.4; book not on file)

T1.text: finite propagation speed and uniqueness for the wave equation with smooth data

T3.text: the massless scalar two-point function is the boundary value of -1/(4 pi^2 z^2) from the forward tube

T4.text: compactly supported Poincare lemma in a ball; Helmholtz decomposition of symmetric tensors in Fourier space

T5.text: first and second variation of area and volume of a hypersurface (used for the displacement quadratic form)
